$comment: Canonical map of every surface this test app contributes to a Horizon host: SDK zone extensions, full-page routes, and one dynamic table column. Single source of truth shared by the app (src/integration/zones.js drives registration from it) and the netsapiens-horizon-testing Playwright suite (asserts each testId mounts). testId scheme: extensions 'sdk-testapp-ext-<id minus the app prefix>', routes 'sdk-testapp-page-<slug>', columns 'sdk-testapp-col-<field>'. Each injected extension is also tagged with data-zone. The testId + data-zone ride on each widget's OWN root element (no wrapper), so the marker is a real, visible box — assert VISIBILITY (toBeVisible). A component that renders null (an inactive zone) has no marker, which is the accurate signal. 'version' mirrors package.json and is the value to register the app under: the remote entry URL is stable, so the registered version is the only thing that tells Horizon to re-verify the bytes at that URL.
$zoneCoverage: All 12 INJECTABLE zones in the host catalogue (SDKSettings.tsx ZONE_CATALOGUE). The other 5 catalogue entries are Navigation zones, which are not injection points — they gate which nav sections an app may add PAGES to, and are covered by 'routes' below. nav-marketplace is reserved to the built-in marketplace and can never be covered by a third-party app.

extensions.label: Side-tray section
extensions.$note: Not covered by horizon-sdk-demo — this zone had no test coverage before the testapp cutover.

extensions.label: Inbound-call content card
extensions.$state: Requires a live ringing call to render — the suite marks this fixme rather than faking call state.

columns.$note: The host's DataTable derives the `call-logs-columns` zone from the route and merges registered columns into the grid. `table-columns` is the catalogue's name for the capability; `call-logs-columns` is the concrete zone id the host emits for this page.
